What makes this one worth it

  • Up to two hours in Amber Fort
  • Jal Mahal photo stop on Man Sagar Lake
  • City Palace and the 19 instruments of the Jantar Mantar
  • Hawa Mahal and the painted arches of Patrika Gate

Your tour schedule

  1. 9:00 AM

    Pickup

    Your driver and guide collect you from your Jaipur hotel.

  2. 9:30 AM

    Amber Fort

    Up to two hours in the hilltop fort's courtyards, halls and mirror work.

  3. 12:30 PM

    Jal Mahal

    A photo stop at the Lake Palace from the lakeside.

  4. 1:00 PM

    Lunch

    Lunch at a local restaurant — Indian, Rajasthani or continental.

  5. 2:00 PM

    City Palace

    The palace built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II between 1729 and 1732, with its museums and courtyards.

  6. 3:30 PM

    Jantar Mantar

    The UNESCO-listed observatory — 19 instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial.

  7. 4:30 PM

    Hawa Mahal

    The Palace of Winds, built so the royal women could watch the street unseen.

  8. 5:00 PM

    Patrika Gate and drop-off

    A photo stop at the painted Patrika Gate, then back to your hotel.

Questions people ask

Is this a private tour?
Yes. Your AC car, driver and licensed English-speaking guide are reserved only for your group, with pickup from your hotel or the airport in Jaipur.
How long does the Jaipur city tour last?
About 8 hours, usually from a 9:00 AM pickup to around 5:00 PM, including sightseeing, a lunch break and hotel pick-up and drop-off.
Are monument entrance tickets included?
Yes. All monument tickets are included in the price, and your guide handles them at each gate so you skip the ticket queue.
Is this tour suitable for families and senior travelers?
Yes. With a private car, a flexible pace and walking kept to a minimum, the day suits families with children and older travellers alike.
What should I wear during the Jaipur city tour?
Choose comfortable, light clothes and walking shoes, as Amber Fort has slopes and steps. Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees is best for forts, palaces and temples.
Can we go inside Jal Mahal?
No, the Lake Palace is not open to visitors, so it is a photo stop from the lakeside promenade. Your guide will point out the best angle, and the light is lovely around midday when we pass.
How do we get up to Amber Fort?
Most guests walk up the stone path from the lake, which takes about 15 minutes at an easy pace, or take a jeep, paid locally since it is not included. Your guide will suggest whichever suits your group best.
Will we be taken to shops along the way?
Only if you ask. We never force shopping stops, and if you would like to see block printing, gems or textiles, your guide can add a stop at a place that makes its own work.
Where do we have lunch, and are there vegetarian options?
Your guide suggests a clean local restaurant serving Indian, Rajasthani or continental food, and vegetarian dishes are easy to find everywhere in Jaipur. Lunch is not included, so you order and pay for what you like.
